documentation.content:
The prod worker returned more than 5 HTTP 5xx responses in a 5-minute window.

THRESHOLD IS MEASURED, NOT GUESSED. A 7-day census of `run.googleapis.com/request_count` at `response_code_class=5xx` on 2026-08-11 gave this distribution of 5-minute buckets: 496 buckets with exactly 1, three with 2, two with 3, one with 4, then 7/8/8/12/7. **Every bucket above 5 fell inside the 2026-08-11 P0 window (16:10Z-16:55Z). Zero on any other day in 7 days.** So `>5 per 5 min` is a zero-false-positive threshold against real history and still fires on the real incident.

KNOWN BACKGROUND, DELIBERATELY UNDER THE THRESHOLD: the service emits a steady ~1 5xx every ~20 minutes around the clock (496 of the 510 non-zero buckets in 7 days). That drip is NOT alerted here on purpose -- it would page ~70 times a week and drown this signal. It is a real open question worth its own investigation, not something to page on.

TRIAGE: check the PGRST002 and lock-wait alerts first -- a database-layer barrier surfaces here as a 5xx burst, and those two alarms name the cause directly. Then Cloud Run logs and Sentry for the same window.
